Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to connect earlier. As promised, attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options that balance predictability and runway flexibility. High level summary below; full line-item pricing and activation rules are in the attached PDF and CSV.

Executive summary (3 options):

1) Safety Lane (Conservative) — 8 GPU reserved baseline + 8 GPU burst pool
   - Minimum guaranteed: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs
   - Burst: up to additional 8 GPUs (best-effort, <30% of peak latency SLO)
   - Ramp: immediate activation (2-week warm-up), full commit after 90 days
   - Monthly committed spend estimate: $42,000

2) Balanced Slate (Recommended) — 16 GPU reserved + 16 GPU burst
   - Minimum guaranteed: 16 GPUs (H100 for latency-critical models)
   - Burst: additional 16 GPUs available with 24/7 SLA priority
   - Ramp: 4-week staged activation (8 -> 12 -> 16), with canary routing
   - Monthly committed spend estimate: $79,000

3) Throughput Anchor (Aggressive) — 32 GPU reserved, immediate throughput headroom
   - Minimum guaranteed: 32 GPUs (H100 mix)
   - Burst: negotiated dedicated burst windows for predictable throughput
   - Ramp: phased across 60 days with runway credits for early-stage scaling
   - Monthly committed spend estimate: $145,000

Key protections and contract carve-outs:
- Escape hatch: 30% downscale allowance at the 6-month mark with 60-day notice (prorata termination credits apply).
- Warm pool credits: first 30 days of warm pool usage are offset for new customers for Balanced and Throughput offers.
- Activation SLA: typical warm-up is 7–21 days depending on model footprint; H100 provisioning may extend to 21 days in some regions.
- Fallback policy: automatically route to a lower-cost model variant (quantized) if capacity constrained; customer opt-in.

Technical notes: Karthik and Neha are looped in for throughput estimates, memory footprints, and prewarm cadence. The attached CSV has a per-model GPU-per-concurrency sizing matrix.

Next steps: please confirm which option you prefer and your target activation quarter. If it helps, we can run a short 2-week pilot on a Balanced Slate with optional conversion credits applied to the reserved contract.

Attachments: veridian_proposal_v1.pdf, capacity_matrix_v1.csv

Hi Alex —

Quick technical context to help the CFO / procurement framing.

Minimum practical reserve: operationally we like to see at least 12 GPUs for production-grade latency-sensitive inference when using small-to-mid models with 2–4 token/response concurrency. Below that, you lose efficient batching and KV cache stability and your p95 latency can vary. So:
- Practical floor: 12 GPUs (H100-equivalent recommended)
- Minimal safe baseline if cost-constrained: 8 GPUs (with tight QoS and aggressive caching; p95 may be 10–30% worse).

H100 lead times and alternatives: 
- H100 inventory varies by region; provisioning lead time can be 7–21 days.
- If you need faster activation, we can provision a mixed pool (A100 + H100) for the first 30–45 days and then migrate to H100 as capacity becomes available — the runtime transparently routes workload.

Burst billing: we offer two burst pricing patterns (you pick at contract):
1) On-demand billing (baseline + on-demand for burst) — simple but can be expensive if bursts are frequent.
2) Tiered burst credits — you purchase a small burst allowance at a blended rate and pay on-demand above that; this smooths CFO exposure.

Escape hatch math (example):
- If you commit to 16 GPUs monthly at $79k/mo and downsize 30% at month 6, we apply a prorated credit on the remaining committed months equal to the unused portion of the committed GPU-hours minus a 12% operational settlement fee. Exact numbers will be spelled out in the term sheet.

I've attached the capacity_matrix_v1.csv with per-model GPU footprints and a sample monthly burn schedule for the Balanced Slate.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your finance team to walk through the termination example.

Thanks —
